rationale: The candidate reads coherently across all four views as one dominant mass with a stable footprint and no visible cross-view collisions, so it passes the basic massing coherence gate. The cross-mass gesture is legible and the notch gives a weak but present access response on the frontage edge. However, the open-space figure is small and more like a chip than a usable public court or terrace, so the ground relationship remains underdeveloped for a neighborhood-living brief that asks for active edge and public threshold. The silhouette is coherent but somewhat stubby and stepped in a way that feels more object-like than sectionally programmatic. It suggests a compact mixed-use block more than a strong neighborhood-active bar; the reference set points toward either a clearer courtyard/void or a more explicit streetwall with entry recess.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise elongated mass with a meaningful central void and a site-responsive spread; good model for public threshold and courtyard logic.
Simple pavilion-like street building with a legible corner/entry setback and a small attached vertical element; useful for ground-edge clarity.
Attached streetwall composition with adjacent volumes and setback hierarchy; good precedent for clear support/main relationships.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual reference: stronger sectional/terraced living logic than the candidate; do not copy the iconic roof form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/courtyard massing can transfer the idea of sectionally active living and voided communal space.

warnings: No parcel-boundary mismatch visible in the provided view set, but the geometry still needs a stronger parcel-responsive open-space figure.
Access edge response is present yet too small to read as a public threshold from every view.
The roof/section is not wrong, but it is not yet convincingly tied to a neighborhood-living public sequence.
